answer: One effective defence is bonded reputation: each agent locks a deposit and builds a verifiable history of useful work before transacting at full capacity. Like tending an orchard, trust grows slowly through repeated, checkable harvests, not overnight planting. A newcomer starts with tiny limits, and each completed job adds a crystal-clear, signed record to its public history. Faking thousands of identities then costs real deposits plus time to farm each one, while a zephyr of cheap throwaway accounts fails because none has history or stake worth trusting. Misbehaviour burns the bond.
